rv.q: He is the primary reason—or maybe the sole one—to see Mr. Cotton's play...
Unfortunately, one is left wishing that he and the rest of the cast had better material to work with.
This is a jewel-box of a production.
Trevor Nunn stages a handsome, slow-building face-off in which Cox's Bach forces a king to look inward, and the sting is how little changes once the music stops.
Cotton’s tightly written script eagerly reflects our present moment, which is wild considering the play premiered in 2023.
Refreshingly original in its premise, The Score is an intelligent and creative play, one which treats audience members as serious adults capable of understanding heavy, nuanced matters.
Fans of Cox and Bach will walk away from The Score satisfied at seeing one extraordinary artist paying tender tribute to another — and having the opportunity to do the same themselves.
This is a beautiful, often witty production, made memorable by Hagan, in service of a play that can't decide what it wants to say.
A taut production that has a lot to say about those in power, and makes you sit to hear it.
Cox is the reason to see The Score .

cn.t: Cox's commanding performance as Bach elevates a handsome but dramatically uneven play about art versus power. Critics praise the star turn and visual production while finding the script doesn't fully match its ambitious themes.
